# Tako

> Tako is a data intelligence platform. The Tako MCP server lets AI agents search a proprietary, continuously-updated knowledge base of 100K+ curated charts — carrying the latest reported quarter, same-day market prices, and official releases as they publish, not static historical reference — get grounded answers, explore Tako's data graph, fetch underlying source content, and run a multi-step Answer Agent. It is a hosted remote MCP server on Cloudflare Workers.

## Documentation

- [MCP Server Setup](https://github.com/TakoData/tako-mcp): Connect to the hosted Tako MCP server
- [API Reference](https://tako.com/docs/): Full REST API documentation
- [Chart Gallery](https://tako.com/gallery): Browse example charts and visualizations
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tako.com/openapi.yaml): Machine-readable API specification

## Connecting

Hosted endpoint: `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). The ChatGPT app uses its own OAuth-only surface at `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp/chatgpt`.

- No token needed: paste the URL and sign in when the client prompts — a per-host key is minted automatically, and a new account gets up to 2,000 free requests. Anonymous connections work immediately: `tako_search` runs (rate-limited, shared capacity); every other tool stays listed and answers with sign-in instructions when called.
- CI, headless runs, and clients without an OAuth flow: pass `Authorization: Bearer <TAKO_API_KEY>` on the same URL. Get a key at tako.com/console/api-keys.

Choosing tools: `?tools=` on the endpoint URL is an ALLOWLIST that REPLACES the default listing, so name every tool you want in one comma-separated list. Tokens are tool names with the `tako_` prefix optional, e.g. `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?tools=search,available_data,contents,agent`. Listed by default: `tako_search`, `tako_available_data`, `tako_contents`, `tako_graph_related`. Opt-in, so reachable only by naming them: `tako_search_advanced` (the whole v3 search body, plus `include_answer` for one synthesized, citation-backed answer and `output_schema` for structured output; `?tools=answer` still resolves to it), `tako_agent` (the multi-step Answer Agent), `tako_visualize` (listed by default on `/mcp/chatgpt`, the surface whose host renders its chart widget inline). Unknown tokens are ignored, and a param that names nothing recognizable serves the defaults, so a typo never breaks the connection. `/mcp/chatgpt` ignores the param: its listing is fixed at submission.

Tools are discovered at runtime via `tools/list`. There is no per-call `api_token` argument — auth is connection-level.

## Available Tools

### Getting values vs. getting pointers

Two tools, one step apart — `tako_search` locates, `tako_contents` reads:

- **Recon and fan-outs**: `tako_search`. Cards carry headline values, node ids, and chart links. Cheap; fire many narrow one-entity+one-metric queries in parallel and assemble the result yourself. The top card auto-renders inline as a chart.
- **The values themselves**: `tako_contents` on an `exportable: true` card's url — the card's rows, up to 2,000, billed per 1k delivered.
- **A web page's text**: `tako_contents` on the web result's url.

Never send a broad or multi-part question as one call — split it into narrow entity+metric searches (e.g. "US CPI inflation", "US core CPI inflation", "US PCE inflation", "US core PCE inflation"). For open-ended, multi-step research use `tako_agent` (opt-in).

### tako_search
Reconnaissance and chart retrieval across Tako's data graph and the live web, returned as structured `cards` plus `web_results`; the top card auto-renders inline as a chart (interactive widget on the ChatGPT app surface, chart image elsewhere). It locates data; `tako_contents` reads it. Cards carry headline values, node ids and chart links — right for breadth (many narrow queries fanned out in parallel to see what exists), for a chart when the embed is the deliverable, and to harvest node ids and urls.

Built to fan out: each query should resolve one metric — for one entity, or a comparison set ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin") — and many narrow queries fired in parallel retrieve far better than one query carrying several metrics or topics. To see what proprietary data exists — or confirm a specific figure exists before you spend a query — check `tako_available_data` first (free), then search on the EXACT canonical name it returns. For a card's rows call `tako_contents` — only when the card is marked `exportable: true`. A non-exportable card (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) carries no rows on any path: read its headline value from the card's `description` when it carries one. Repeated source/methodology paragraphs are hoisted out of the cards into the trailing Source notes section, and metric definitions into Definitions — both keyed by a card's `source` field verbatim, so look that string up there (truncating clients lose boilerplate before data). For open-ended research use `tako_agent` (opt-in). Results arrive as a markdown document, in this order: a `>` guidance line when nothing matched, `## Data cards` (per card: headline, exportable flag, node ids, url), a `Top card chart —` line carrying the embed and image urls, `## Web results`, `## Definitions`, `## Source notes`, and a usage footer. On `tako_search_advanced`, `include_answer` puts the answer first, above everything else, and adds `## Structured output` (or a `>` line naming why it is absent) and `## Related queries`; this tool emits none of those three. This tool never inlines rows — a card's rows are a `tako_contents` call on its url, and only when it is `exportable: true`. The markdown is COMPLETE, not an index: every field the structured payload carries — web-result snippets included — renders there too, because many hosts feed the model only that channel.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one metric, on one entity or a comparison set; parallelize multiple. Wrap a multi-word name in double quotes to keep it one entity (`"tesla motors" club revenue`), and append `:LABEL` to force its type (`"Tesla":PRODUCT price`; PERSON, ORG, GPE, LOC, PRODUCT, DATE, EVENT, MONEY, CARDINAL, METRIC, TIME_PERIOD, UNITS). Tako strips the quotes before it searches. An unpaired quote disables quoting for the whole query — silently, so check both marks — a quoted phrase caps at 80 characters, and an unknown label stays in the query text.
- `sources` (array): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for live web only.
- `country_code` (string, optional): ISO country code. Omit it for the server default, US.
- `locale` (string, optional): Locale. Omit it for the server default, en-US.

Four parameters, and it declares no defaults of its own: an omitted field is omitted from the request, so the server's default applies. The one exception is `highlights` on the web source, always on, so each snippet carries the query-relevant passages rather than the page's opening characters. For a per-source result count, inline rows, a graph pin, a web domain filter, or `effort: deep`, use `tako_search_advanced` (opt-in, `?tools=search_advanced`).

### tako_search_advanced
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=search_advanced` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). It exposes the v3 `POST /api/v3/search` body WHOLE: every field of the request and of both source blocks, derived from the published schema. The top level and both source blocks are strict, so a field the API does not have is an error rather than a silent drop. Use `tako_search` unless you need an option it does not carry: a per-source result count, inline card rows, a graph pin, a web domain or category filter, or the `deep` effort tier. Nothing is sent unless you set it, with one exception — web `highlights` defaults to true here, and `web: {"highlights": false}` turns it off. Naming a source block — even as an empty object — is what selects that source; omit both and the server searches data and web. The structured payload is `tako_search`'s plus the four fields only this tool can produce — `answer`, `structured_output`, `structured_output_error` and `related`; `tako_search` declares none of them, because it cannot reach the answer endpoint. The other difference is that this tool does not auto-render the top card as an inline chart, so read `embed_url` for the chart. This is also the values channel for non-exportable cards: when a search card is `exportable: false` (usually license-gated), re-ask here with that card's METRIC node id ALONE (the `mt::` entry in its `nodes`) in `data.node_ids`, `strict: true`, and `data.include_contents: true` — pinning every node id on the card re-admits its other cards, and omitting `strict` only boosts, which measured as not enough to land the metric.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one metric per query retrieves best, the same as on the simple tool, and the same quoting syntax applies.
- `effort` (string, "fast" | "instant" | "deep", optional): Omit for the server default (fast). "instant" serves cached embeds without a new retrieval; "deep" widens retrieval and adds an LLM rerank — slower, and billed at a premium tier.
- `country_code` (string, optional): ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Omit for the server default, US.
- `locale` (string, optional): BCP-47 tag. Omit for the server default, en-US.
- `location` (object, optional): `{latitude, longitude}` of the end user, for implicit-location queries such as weather. An explicit location in the query wins.
- `timezone` (string, optional): IANA timezone (for example `America/New_York`) for resolving relative dates.
- `output_settings` (object, optional): `image_dark_mode` for card preview images; `force_refresh` is informational on these endpoints.
- `include_related` (integer 1-20, optional): Return up to N follow-up query suggestions in `related`. Omit to disable.
- `include_answer` (boolean, optional): Set true to run the answer endpoint (`POST /api/v1/answer`) instead of search — one synthesized, citation-backed answer in `answer`, with the retrieved cards and web results as its citations. Every other option applies the same way.
- `output_schema` (object, optional): JSON Schema to fill from the same evidence as the answer, returned in `structured_output`. Requires `include_answer: true`; sending it without that is rejected before any request goes out.
- `data` (object, optional): Tako data source settings — `count` (1-20; server default 5), `include_contents` (server default false), `max_rows` (omit for your account's inline cap, up to the 2,000-row ceiling), `content_format` (`json_compact` | `json_records` | `csv` | `card_json`), `node_ids` (up to 20 graph node ids to pin), `strict` (hard filter over the pinned nodes), `mode` (a documented no-op for Tako cards). To land on exactly one metric, pin THAT metric's node id alone with `strict: true` and name the entity in the query text; adding the entity's own id widens the filter back out. If that call returns 0 cards, drop `node_ids` and run the query text alone — the graph holds near-duplicate metric nodes where only one twin carries cards.
- `web` (object, optional): Web source settings — `count` (1-20; server default 5), `include_contents` (page text; server default false), `include_domains` / `exclude_domains` (bare hosts, max 20 each), `category` (`news` | `sports` | `finance`), `snippet_max_chars` (server default 4000), `highlights` (query-relevant passages instead of the page opening; this tool defaults it to true — set false for the page opening), `published_after` / `published_before` (ISO dates bounding the page's publish date), `article_content_max_chars` (cap on the inlined page text `include_contents` returns; server default 30000).

### tako_contents
Fetch the real content behind result URLs (1-10 per call) from `tako_search` — the rows behind a Tako card (CSV by default, or JSON), or a web page's full text. Requires a signed-in connection; anonymous calls return sign-in instructions. It is the step after search when you need the full data to compute over or quote. Batch them: fetching 8 pages in one call costs the same as 8 calls but saves 7 round trips, and every extra round trip re-sends the whole conversation as input tokens.

Precondition (Tako cards): non-exportable cards (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) always 403 — never call this on them; their headline value is in the card's `description` (when present). Call only on `exportable: true` cards, and even then a rare card still 403s: read the headline instead, don't retry. Web URLs always work.

Parameters:
- `urls` (array of string, 1-10): The result URLs to fetch — a Tako card's `url`, web-result URLs, or a mix. Each is fetched and BILLED independently and one URL failing does not fail the others (its entry carries an `error` instead of a payload). Results are returned in `results`, positionally aligned with the URLs you passed.
- `url` (string, optional): Deprecated single-URL form, equivalent to `urls: [url]`. Prefer `urls`. Pass one or the other; if you send both, `urls` wins.
- `content_format` (string, optional): Tako cards only — serialization of the data: `csv` (default, text in `data`), `json_records` (row objects in `records`), or `json_compact` (compact columns+rows in `dataset`). Ignored for web URLs (always text).
- `max_rows` (integer, 1-2000, optional): Tako cards only — max rows to return (billed per 1k rows). Omit it to get the whole card, up to the 2,000-row ceiling; set it lower to spend less. Ignored for web URLs (use `max_chars`).
- `max_chars` (integer, 1-1,000,000, optional): Web URLs only — character cap on the extracted page text (1,000,000 = full text). Inline fetches default to 100,000; billing is per page regardless, so the cap only trims what reaches you (`truncated: true` reports a cut). Raise it toward 1,000,000 for a full long document inline. In url mode the downloaded file is the full text unless you set this (an explicit value caps the file too). Ignored when `query` is set (passages always scan the full text) and for Tako card URLs (use `max_rows`).
- `query` (string, optional): Web URLs + inline mode only — return just the passages around case-insensitive matches of this query (full phrase first, per-word fallback) instead of the full page text; one call lands on the relevant section of a long page, and the full text is always scanned regardless of `max_chars`. The `note` field summarizes the matches; a no-match note says so explicitly (a deterministic miss — try another url, not another wording). Ignored for Tako card URLs and in url mode.
- `mode` (string, "inline" | "url", default "inline"): Delivery only, not row count — `inline` returns the data in the response so you can read it; `url` returns a short-lived presigned `download_url` to the same file.

### tako_available_data
Find what proprietary, continuously-updated structured data exists on something — summarized in one call. Free and fast. Ask it when the question IS coverage: what does Tako have on X, is this measure tracked at all, what is it called — then build the real question around what comes back. Worth one call when you need a measure's EXACT name, since resolving it to the canonical form measurably improves what the priced call retrieves. Works on an entity (a company, person, or place → the metrics tracked on it, e.g. Tesla) or a metric (→ the entities it is tracked across, e.g. Inflation Rate), reported as a natural-language summary you can show the user.

Two paths, chosen by whether you pass `metric`:
- **Lookup** (`q` + `metric`, e.g. `q="Carnival", metric="passenger cruise days"`) — resolves the entity+metric PAIR directly in ~0.6s and returns a runnable `next_call`. Use it whenever you already know the measure.
- **Discovery** (`q` alone) — lists what the resolved node covers, for browsing. Candidate names are relevance-gated against `q` (name matches rank above alias matches), so a fuzzy graph hit about a different company is not reported as coverage.
- **Both kinds** — when `q` alone names an entity and a metric ("US core PCE" → the company Core and the metric Core PCE Price Index), the tool returns both as candidates (subtype, label, aliases, coverage count) and renders neither. Re-run with `types` or `metric`.
- **Browse filter** — `metric` is sent as the API's substring filter on the entity's metrics, so `q="Nvidia", metric="data center"` returns every matching metric with its node id, not a 25-name sample.

The exact metric/entity names are the terms to reuse in the follow-up call; `structuredContent.matches[].coverage.items[]` pairs each name with its `node_id`. Search on the EXACT name returned — the canonical name is what recovers cards, and `tako_search` takes no pin. A `node_id` is for `tako_graph_related` traversal, not for the search call. When the measure is known, `next_call` is that follow-up prewritten — run it verbatim.

A broad entity's coverage list is capped and may be truncated: treat a name you don't see as UNCONFIRMED rather than absent. This tool confirms a name EXISTS in the graph; it cannot confirm a chart exists behind it — the `next_call` is that check, and if it comes back with 0 cards, report the gap rather than rephrasing: one retrieval on the canonical name is the best free evidence available, not proof of absence. On the discovery path, `found: true` means a match has live coverage, never that a name merely resolved; on the lookup path it means the entity holds something matching, and `verified` says what was checked. `found: false` is a real answer: report the gap rather than silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `q` (string, required, min 2 chars): The NAME of the entity (or metric) to look up. Put the measure in `metric`, not here.
- `metric` (string, optional, min 2 chars): The measure you want, when you already know it — e.g. "gross margin", "capex". Supplying it selects the fast lookup path above.
- `types` (string, "entity" | "metric", optional): Narrow resolution to a thing ("entity") or a measure ("metric"); omit to search both.
- `label` (string, optional): NER label to prefer — a boost, not a filter. Supply it when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, country→GPE, person→PERSON, metric→METRIC, …). Describes the ENTITY only; it is not applied to `metric`.
- `limit` (integer, 1–20, optional, default 10): How many candidate nodes to resolve. Every candidate comes back with its node id, type, subtype, label, and aliases; only the top few are coverage-checked.

### tako_graph_related
Listed by default. Explore what a graph node connects to — the map of what data Tako has for it. Free. Covers what `tako_available_data` does not: traversal relations (siblings, part_of, members, `rel:*` named edges like `rel:competes_with`), server-side `q` filtering within a relation, and cursor paging past the first page. Overview (`node_id` alone) is a compact map — each relation group's `key`, `label`, `total`, and its first three items. Drill (`relation: "<key>"`) pages one group; items carry `id`, `name`, `type`, `subtype`, `label`, and only the focal node carries aliases and a truncated description. `q` is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING match on names and aliases, one string per call. A listed metric is table-level evidence, not proof — `tako_search` is the final validator. Empty `items` is a normal answer: report the gap instead of silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `node_id` (string, required): Node id from `tako_available_data` or a card's `nodes`.
- `relation` (string, optional): Relation key to page — metrics, entities, siblings, part_of, members, or rel:<phrase>. Omit for the overview.
- `q` (string, optional): Case-insensitive substring filter on name+aliases — one string per call; for several name-variants of a metric ("revenue", "sales"), call once per variant.
- `label` (string, optional) / `infer_label` (boolean, optional): NER label to prefer when resolving — a boost, not a filter.
- `cursor` (string, optional) / `limit` (integer, 1-100, default 50): Pagination within a drilled relation.

### tako_visualize
Opt-in tool — name `visualize` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Listed by default on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`), which renders its chart inline as a widget; everywhere else enable it for the shareable embed URL. Create an embeddable Tako card from your OWN structured data (not from search), backed by Tako's Thin-Viz API. Provide one or more typed components; the card auto-renders inline as a chart and returns share/embed URLs.

Parameters:
- `components` (array, required): One or more `{ component_type, config, component_variant? }` objects. `component_type` is one of: header, generic_timeseries, categorical_bar, choropleth, data_table_chart, histogram, pie, table, financial_boxes, timeline, treemap, heatmap, marimekko, boxplot, waterfall, sankey, scatter, bubble, top_level_metric, person_card. `config` holds that type's data (validated server-side). The optional `component_variant` string selects a type variant (e.g. 'simple', 'financial'). `person_card` must be the only component.
- `title` (string, optional): Card title
- `description` (string, optional): Card description
- `source` (string, optional): Data source attribution shown in the footer
- `height` (integer, 100-2000, optional): Chart height in pixels
- `normalize_currencies` (string, optional): Target ISO 4217 code to convert currency-denominated datasets

### tako_agent
Opt-in tool — name `agent` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Run Tako's Answer Agent for open-ended, multi-step questions whose shape needs figuring out — cohorts, ranking or filtering by criteria, aggregation, and multi-hop reasoning across many entities; also the fallback when `tako_search` / `tako_search_advanced` return nothing. Returns a synthesized answer plus supporting chart cards (~30–90s). Not on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`): that host sends no progressToken, so a polled run cannot stay inside its per-call timeout.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): The open-ended, analytical question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for open-web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `thread_id` (string UUID, optional): Continue a prior agent run's thread as a follow-up; omit to start a new thread.
